content: Nephritis refers to the inflammation of the kidney. The term is derived from the Greek word nephromeaning of the kidney and the suffix -itis, which signifies inflammation. This condition is frequently caused by infections, exposure to toxins, or autoimmune diseases. Subtypes of Nephritis: Glomerulonephritis: This is the inflammation of the glomeruli, which are the tiny filtering units within the kidney. When the term nephritis is used without further specification, it often refers to this particular condition. Interstitial Nephritis (or Tubulo-Interstitial Nephritis): This subtype involves inflammation of the spaces between the renal tubules, which are the structures responsible for filtering and reabsorbing substances in the kidney. Pyelonephritis: This occurs when a urinary tract infection progresses to involve the renal pelvis (pyelum) of the kidney, leading to inflammation. Lupus Nephritis: This is a form of kidney inflammation caused by systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues, including the kidneys.
